title: RNA Extraction from Tigriopus californicus Copepods
author: Isabelle Neylan

steps.title: Sample Preparation
steps.instruction: Retrieve frozen samples from -80°C and place them in an icebox, moving them one at a time.

steps.title: Copepod Crushing
steps.instruction: Crush the frozen copepods in the presence of RLT buffer and TRIZOL.

substeps.instruction: Add 50uL of RLT buffer to each sample tube immediately.
Grind copepods with a tissue ruptor for 30 to 60 seconds until no intact copepods remain and the liquid looks pulpy.
Add 1000uL of TRIZOL reagent to each tube (total TRIZOL per sample is 1000uL).
Keep tubes on ice while working through samples, though crushing can occur off ice if copepods are submerged in TRIZOL.

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the RNA from DNA and proteins using chloroform and centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Incubate tubes at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Add 200uL of chloroform to each tube.
Shake thoroughly for a couple of minutes until the solution turns a light pink shade.
Incubate at room temperature for 3 minutes.
Centrifuge at 4°C for 15 minutes at 13,000 rpm.

steps.title: RNA Recovery and gDNA Removal
steps.instruction: Isolate the aqueous RNA layer and remove genomic DNA using a spin column.

substeps.instruction: Maintain the tube at a 45-degree angle and gently pipette the upper transparent RNA layer (typically 300-400uL) using a 200uL pipette (set to 180uL, usually 2-2.5 pulls).
Transfer the RNA layer onto a Qiagen gDNA eliminator spin column in a 2mL collection tube, avoiding the sides of the tube and the pink layer.
Centrifuge the gDNA column at room temperature for 30 seconds at 10,000 rpm.
Discard the column and save the flow-through.

steps.title: RNA Precipitation and Binding
steps.instruction: Precipitate the RNA and bind it to an RNeasy spin column.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 volume of 70% ethanol to the flow-through (typically 380uL) and mix well by pipetting; do not centrifuge.
Transfer up to 700uL of the sample (including any precipitate) to an RNeasy spin column in a 2mL collection tube.
Centrifuge for 30 seconds at 10,000 rpm and discard the flow-through.
If the sample volume exceeds 700uL, centrifuge successive aliquots in the same column, discarding flow-through after each centrifugation.

steps.title: Column Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the RNeasy spin column to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Add 700uL Buffer RW1 to the column, centrifuge for 30 seconds at 10,000 rpm, and discard flow-through.
Add 500uL Buffer RPE (ensure ethanol was added to the concentrate) to the column, centrifuge for 30 seconds at 10,000 rpm, and discard flow-through.
Add 500uL Buffer RPE to the column and centrifuge for 2 minutes at 10,000 rpm to dry the membrane.
Carefully remove the column from the collection tube after centrifugation to avoid contact with flow-through.

steps.title: Final Drying and Elution
steps.instruction: Ensure the column is dry and elute the purified RNA.

substeps.instruction: Place the RNeasy spin column in a new 2mL collection tube and centrifuge at full speed for 1 minute to eliminate residual Buffer RPE.
Place the column in a new 1.5mL collection tube.
Add 40uL RNase-free water directly to the membrane and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at 10,000 rpm to elute the RNA.

steps.title: Storage and Quality Control
steps.instruction: Immediately stabilize the extracted RNA and prepare for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Immediately place eluted tubes on ice.
Aliquot 1uL of freshly extracted RNA into PCR strip tubes for RIN analysis if required.
Store RNA samples in a -80°C freezer; avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles.
